A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same behavioral game-theoretic evaluation of LLM strategic reasoning. Their main texts, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable matching despite extensive reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original LLM game experiments, reasoning-depth estimates for 22 models, CoT comparisons, and demographic regressions in Tables 2–5.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experiments and additionally reports reasoning-trace analyses, completion-token statistics, gamma estimates, and likelihood results.

M1.justification: The game–prompt–TQRE–MLE pipeline remains, but its written belief-aggregation rule changes. v1 multiplies strategies across lower reasoning levels; v3 uses a normalized Poisson-weighted mixture and multiplies across opponents. This corrects the specified expected-utility computation, although the PDFs do not establish an implementation change or rerun.

E1.justification: The same game families, payoff matrices, SW10 human-comparison task, and demographic dimensions remain. The added reasoning-trace and fit analyses reuse existing games. Finer reported persona categories concern experimental settings rather than a demonstrated expansion into new tasks or populations.

E2.justification: Although the main 22-model comparisons remain, the SW10 comparison contracts from 29 LLM configurations in v1 Figure 5 to 12 in v3 Figure 3, removing all distilled variants and most CoT variants, including GPT-4o-CoT. v3 Section 3.4 also introduces a uniform-chance comparator for likelihood diagnostics.

E3.justification: v3 adds a substantial trace-analysis protocol involving anonymization, a predefined coding rubric, independent overlapping coding, and completion-token measurement, alongside likelihood-versus-chance diagnostics. Table 6 also reports finer age and education categories than v1 Table 1, without establishing that experiments were rerun. Existing game matrices and prompt templates remain unchanged.

E4.justification: New analyses examine three leading models’ reasoning styles and token use, plus Claude-3-Opus and GPT-4o case studies explaining contrasting CoT effects, with complete traces in Appendix E. Fit diagnostics are also added. Earlier distillation and CoT–demographic analyses survive in Appendix B rather than being removed.

E5.justification: v3 Table 8 newly reports mean, minimum, and maximum completion-token counts, adding descriptive information about variability across trials. The existing 30-trial count, regression standard errors, and significance thresholds remain unchanged; no new seed information or confidence intervals for reasoning-depth estimates are supplied.

E6.justification: The original reasoning-depth and demographic regression values are retained, but v3 adds gamma, likelihood, completion-token, and qualitative reasoning results in Tables 4–5, 8, 10, and 13. GPT-o1’s leading-game count changes from four to six, correctly including ties. The human-outperformance count changes from 17 to six because the displayed comparator set shrinks, not because matching scores demonstrate a performance change.

T1.justification: Section 2.2 and new Appendix A replace v1’s non-equivalent product-over-levels formulation with normalized lower-level mixture weights, explicit opponent-independence assumptions, and corresponding joint beliefs and expected utilities. v1’s asserted convergence to Nash equilibrium as tau and gamma increase is also removed. These substantively revise the mathematical foundations.

C1.justification: v3 redefines the second headline contribution around reasoning styles and chain-length analysis, replacing v1’s emphasis on capability-dependent benefits of CoT prompting. Its abstract newly emphasizes identified maximin and belief-based strategies and the limits of longer reasoning chains. The framework, model-scale, and fairness claims remain central.

C2.justification: v3 adds detailed interpretations involving GPT-o1’s defensive maximin reasoning, GPT-o3-mini’s belief-based flexibility, DeepSeek-R1’s strategic trust, and productive self-correction versus redundant reasoning loops. It clarifies gamma as choice precision and adds training-association/RLHF explanations for persona effects. The earlier causal and real-time-interaction limitations remain.

D1.justification: v3 adds trace-collection and coding information, full illustrative traces, and a Poisson-truncation criterion. Conversely, v1’s explicit temperature of 1, top-p of 1, absence of a repetition penalty, and dated GPT-4o identifier disappear. The detailed game matrices and experiment prompt templates remain available.

R1.justification: v3 adds Nash (1950) and Wright and Leyton-Brown (2010), while pruning supporting literature including GameBench, Strategic Chain-of-Thought, and several behavioral-game and agent studies. The central positioning against NE-focused evaluations and deterministic cognitive-hierarchy assumptions remains substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: The title and much of the main narrative are rewritten. LLM-related literature moves into the introduction, theory and experimental setup are reorganized, human/persona analysis receives a separate section, and substantial existing discussion moves into the reorganized appendices. These changes extend well beyond inserting new results.

P2.justification: The framework diagram is redrawn, representative payoff matrices enter the main text, and appendix matrices are consolidated into grouped tables. Distribution plots disappear, demographic bar charts are replaced by a coefficient plot, the human comparison is redrawn, and CoT tables and demographic plots move to Appendix B. New trace, token, gamma, and likelihood tables substantially change the presentation.

improvement.justification: v3 improves mathematical clarity and auditability through corrected belief aggregation, fit diagnostics, and disclosed reasoning traces. However, new demographic claims contradict retained evidence: Section 5 describes positive GPT-4o sexuality effects, whereas Table 11a reports negative bisexual and homosexual coefficients. The claimed Claude calculation correction is also not demonstrated by Appendix E’s repeated calculations, and explicit generation settings are lost. These material reliability and reproducibility costs prevent a confident net quality judgment.
